subject: Service account keys, IP allowlist & VPC peering — sprint plan and MAP checkpoints
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Weber <a.weber@medlytics.com>, Maya Singh <maya@medlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff — service accounts, IP allowlist, VPC peering (next 10 days)

Hi Alex / Maya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great questions from your infra team. Per our MAP commitments, I put together a short sprint plan focused on environment access so you can start evaluation runs this week. High-level ask: can MedLytics provide a service account and an infra contact to validate the VPC peering and IP ranges?

Proposed 10-day checklist (attached):
- Day 0: Service account creation + key exchange (Redwood test account)
- Day 1–2: IP allowlist entries for our egress and control plane
- Day 3–5: VPC peering validation and route table confirmation
- Day 6–9: Smoke tests, sample tokenized workloads, latency checks
- Day 10: Acceptance sign-off and next-step checklist

Deliverables I need from you: service account name, preferred key exchange method (SFTP/Drive/Secrets Manager), and infra contact for peering. I attached a short playbook with preferred RBAC and key rotation guidance.

If you can share the infra contact and a time for a short 30-min peering call tomorrow, I’ll schedule.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai] | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: MAP_Roadmap_v1.pdf, service-account-playbook.md
From: Alex Weber <a.weber@medlytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@medlytics.com>, MedLytics Infra <infra@medlytics.com>
Date: 2027-08-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — service accounts, IP allowlist, VPC peering (next 10 days)

Jordan — thanks for the clear plan. Looping in our infra lead, Raj Patel (infra@medlytics.com), who will own peering. Quick answers:
- Service account: medlytics-eval-redwood (we can create this afternoon)
- Key exchange: we prefer to upload to our secure SFTP and share a one-time token
- IP allowlist: we’ll need your outbound IP ranges (control plane + inference egress)

Raj — can you and your team be available for a 30-min call tomorrow at 11am PT to kick off peering?

Alex
Alex Weber | Director, Platform Engineering | MedLytics
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Patel <infra@medlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-21T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Intro + peering call agenda

Raj — great to meet you over email. 

Agenda for 11am PT call:
1) Confirm service account owner and key delivery method
2) Share Redwood IP ranges (control plane + egress) and required ports
3) Review VPC peering steps and a minimal route table example
4) Agreed test plan and acceptance criteria (smoke tests list)

Internal note: Marissa / Vivek — FYI I’ve asked for the IP ranges and a lightweight route example so MedLytics can validate with their infra. Can you prepare the vpc-peering-template.yaml and a short list of the outbound IPs we expect to use for the evaluation (control-plane: 54.23.11.0/24; egress pool: 35.180.72.0/22) — I’ll share on the call.

Thanks,
Jordan
From: Raj Patel <infra@medlytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Alex Weber <a.weber@medlytics.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@medlytics.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + peering call agenda

Thanks Jordan — quick recap from our call:
- Service account medlytics-eval-redwood created; key uploaded to our SFTP path /incoming/rdw/medlytics-eval (one-time token shared with Jordan via separate SFTP notice)
- We’ve added preliminary allowlist entries for your control plane IPs and egress pool (please confirm exact port range for testing; we opened 443/80 initially)
- Peering: we hit a routing snag where our NAT gateway uses a default route for 35.180.72.0/22; Raj to update route table to prefer peered route.
- Action items: MedLytics to confirm route table change; Redwood to provide final vpc-peering-template.yaml and a quick smoke-test script.

We did one smoke test and saw TLS handshake succeed; awaiting final route change before full test.

—Raj
Raj Patel | Infra Lead | MedLytics
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Weber <a.weber@medlytics.com>, Raj Patel <infra@medlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-25T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: MAP update — acceptance runway & close timeline (RDW-3251)

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Raj / Alex. Status update and next steps to hit acceptance by Day 10:
- MedLytics: confirm route table change and share screenshot of peering status (Expected by EOD 2027-08-25)
- Redwood: final vpc-peering-template.yaml (attached) and smoke-test script; we’ll run a set of 50 sample requests overnight and share metrics in the morning
- Acceptance criteria: 95th p50 token latency under target, successful auth via service account, and stable peering for 24 hours

I’ve attached the vpc-peering-template.yaml and an updated MAP_Roadmap_v1.pdf that shifts one day to allow for the routing rollback we saw. If MedLytics confirms EOD, we’ll schedule sign-off call 2027-08-26 10am PT and propose a 30% evaluation credit on the initial month (internal approval from Marissa confirmed).

Attachments: vpc-peering-template.yaml, MAP_Roadmap_v1.pdf

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
